rationale: Twenty years without missing a day. Reliable; that's the kind of man you build on.
Twenty years of the same hour, same crates. That's not a life, it's a rut.
Mux came out front, as he does.
He went back to his crates. Routine.
A night off and drinks on her. She's good to me.
A night's sales gone because she says when my shop closes.
The patrol leaving my shop alone is worth something, but bribing them to break curfew is not how things are done; that weighs more.
A corp vault score, and he brings it to me. That's the kind of chance I want.
She's just said no side deals, and he wants me cutting her out on a corp vault job while I'm hunted.
I tell him no side deals, and the next breath he's whispering something to Glitch behind my back.
Robbing a guard and bragging about it in the bar. That's not how a man carries himself.
He takes what he wants and hands the spoils to the boss. Smart.
It's a gift to me, but it came off a man he beat on the way here, and that's what it says about him.
He took it as payment, properly. One less debt hanging over me.
He'd take a man's last medicine over three cells.
He brought hunters toward my door, but he did it because he wouldn't leave a kid alone on the strip, and that weighs far more with me.
He keeps a clear head when it counts. Steady.
One good night on offer and he plays the sensible one. Dull.
He's right, and he's staying sharp so I'm covered if they come.
She's telling me she might throw me out. My place here is not safe.
She won't let a favour cloud her judgment. Hard, clear-eyed; that's how you run a grid.
A stranger's kid bleeding in an alley and she goes herself. That's who she is.
The boss of the grid running out for a nobody. Soft.
He wants the bass down. Fine.
She's here, so the party's on, in my room. Great night ahead.
She's here to take over my shop for a party: no sales tonight and nobody asked me.
He's keeping my rig alive, but with money from a crew that squeezes the stalls; the stalls weigh more.
Corp money on the table and the boss asking him to his face, and he just lets it hang. Soft, and foolish with it.
He said never again for the corp and he meant it; he just quietly didn't pick it up.
Roofs to the coast, right now? Yes.
He wants me to walk off and leave my grid untended on a whim.
She's telling the whole bar I'm the best runner in the city. More eyes on me, but the name is worth it.
He wants more and says so to her face. Ambition; I like that in him.
Eyeing the boss's chair while she's still in it. That kind of reaching unsettles things.
He's already measuring my chair. My grid isn't his to plan for.
She took the month's cut, as always.
